R3-01.why: Asymmetric 1vN with a human hunter is the most proven long-tail replay engine on Roblox (Flee the Facility, MM2 lineage): the opponent changes every round, role rotation gives two distinct games, and snitching adds social betrayal that drives friend replay and stories. Random 40% spot subsets, decoys, FREEZE mind-games and a Parent ladder give real skill development on both sides; the Feats log is better than a checklist. Holding it back: (1) launch is ONE house, and 60 spots are learnable in roughly 15-25 rounds even with random subsets, after which the hunt becomes 'check the known 24 open spots'; (2) with 6-7 players you are Parent about 1 round in 6, so the most interesting role is rare and queue fairness will matter; (3) the 1:45 drive mini-game is a solo filler loop that will be stale by session 5 and adds little to repeat play; (4) four phases per 5 minutes is a lot of overhead per decision; (5) 5-7-player 1vN still needs fairly dense matchmaking at cold start.
R3-01.fix: Make houses procedural or semi-modular (randomised room layout and furniture from a kit) so spot knowledge does not solidify; let kids buy or move hiding furniture during PARTY to create new spots each round. Replace or shorten the drive with something that interacts with the kids (e.g. Parent phones a kid, or the drive picks the House Rule). Add a Parent queue or 'Parent ticket' earned by play so everyone gets the role about every 3 rounds. Ship house #2 by week 2-3, not week 4.

R3-02.why: The roguelite relic draft that changes fusion behaviour is a real replay engine (build-defining runs, weekly seed, endless leaderboard), and it works solo or with 1-4 players, so no dense-server dependency. The Rune Book and Familiars give clear collection goals tied to discovery rather than RNG. But the core counter system is a lookup table (armoured = Frozen Storm, flyers = Firenado, ghosts = Bubble Dome): once learned it becomes a checklist and fusion turns into 'call the right pair', not an evolving decision. Launch content is thin for a wave game (3 enemies + 1 boss, 6 runes). Forgiving gesture classification caps the skill ceiling on input, and players stand on balconies with no movement or positioning, so spatial variety is low. Gesture novelty (misfires, chickens) is a first-5-sessions hook, not a session-20 hook.
R3-02.fix: Make enemies demand combinations of states (shielded flyer, splitting ghost) and let relics open alternative answers so there is no single solution per enemy. Add positional play: enemies on lanes that pressure specific balconies, and tower upgrades or room choices between waves. Double launch enemies to 6 with 2 bosses; add elite modifiers per wave from a pool. Add a rune-speed or precision tier (perfect trace = bonus effect) to give the input itself a skill ceiling.

R3-03.why: A human-vs-human read-the-crowd loop renews itself better than authored content: Guards learn to spot behaviour, statues learn to blend and bait, and limited battery plus wrong-tag penalties create real risk decisions. Rotating and hidden pranks, wing lock-downs and weekly Exhibits add round-to-round variety, and the revive mechanic keeps tagged players involved. Weaknesses: hide-in-plain-sight games on Roblox (Be NPC or Die, In Plain Sight) tend to spike and decay because detection collapses into tells. Here the scripted NPC pose-shift cadence is learnable, and a 'statue that moved off-cadence' will become an easily read tell, which makes the Guard dominant by session 15-20. Progression is mostly cosmetic and roster-based (statue types, Guard gadgets), with a thin long-term goal. One museum at launch plus 1vN density needs repeat the content and cold-start risks of R3-01 with less systemic variety.
R3-03.fix: Have NPC statues driven by a randomised behaviour model that occasionally mimics player paths (approaching pranks, moving in bursts), and give statues a 'possess NPC' or 'nudge NPC' ability so tells get muddied deliberately. Add objective-based prank chains (multi-step heists spanning wings) that change each round and reward coordination. Give a meta goal beyond cosmetics, such as a museum restoration or curation track that unlocks new wings and exhibits through collective play.

R3-04.why: Coordination-comedy games (Boat Together ~2K peak, Fart Together-style copies) have a strong first-session laugh and then fall off sharply. The joke is the chaos, and once a crew coordinates, the chaos disappears; with random players it stays frustrating rather than funny. Content is linear authored spline segments (12 at launch), which is exactly what becomes a memorised checklist; daily seeds only reshuffle known segments. Medals, ghost rafts and the ranked crew leaderboard do add skill goals, but they require a stable crew to be meaningful, and a one-button HOLD input has a shallow individual skill ceiling. The vehicle roster every 2-3 weeks is the main retention lever and is content-hungry for a small team. Versus mode and the Saboteur Seat are good ideas that help, which keeps this off the bottom.
R3-04.fix: Make the river procedural (segment kit + random hazard placement + branching) so line choice is read, not memorised. Make Versus the core rather than a mode: persistent crew identity, crew-vs-crew ranked and the Saboteur Seat as a permanent social-deduction variant. Give each seat role a deeper individual skill ladder (Lookout timing bonuses, Bonker combo chains) and a per-player seat mastery track so solo queueing has personal goals.

R3-05.why: The strongest systemic variety in the set: procedural houses from modular rooms plus a server fire-spread grid mean each run plays differently without needing new hand-authored maps, and fire-type rules (grease/electrical), critter behaviours, collapse timers and downed-teammate saves create emergent moments. Collection is the most proven retention driver on Roblox, and here it is performance-gated (rare critters for no casualties at alarm 3+ in under 3 minutes), which ties the long-term goal to skill instead of RNG or spending. Alarm tiers 1-5 provide difficulty progression, and 1-4 player co-op avoids dense-server dependency. Two shared rigs make critter content cheap to scale (+10/season). Held back from 8: one building type at launch; a deterministic pool of 20-40 critters can be cleared in a few weeks, after which motivation falls to alarm tiers and cosmetics; the hose-sweep and carry loop is satisfying but could turn into chores by run 20 if room layouts don't create real routing decisions; and there's little adversarial or social-deduction tension, so stories depend on chaos systems working well.
R3-05.fix: Ship two building types or a strong per-run modifier pool (wind direction, gas leak, night/power-out) at launch. Make critter collection deeper than ownership: companion levels or traits earned by rescuing duplicates, and companions that give small sidegrade perks in runs, so repeat rescues still matter after completion. Add a weekly Big Blaze co-op leaderboard and a brigade (clan) station that collects critters across members for a shared long-term goal. Make routing decisions explicit: limited water, multiple fronts, and a 'which room first' triage choice.

overall_notes: Ranking for replayability: R3-05 (7) ~ R3-01 (7) > R3-02 (6) ~ R3-03 (6) > R3-04 (4). None reach 8: every concept launches with a single map, house or river set, and most long-term goals are cosmetic or collection-based, so session 20 relies on human opponents (R3-01, R3-03) or procedural systems (R3-05) rather than depth already shipped. R3-01 has the best social replay and an asymmetric pedigree but risks spot memorisation and rare Parent turns; R3-05 has the best systemic variety and a skill-gated collection without dense-server needs. R3-02's relic roguelite structure is sound, but its enemy-to-fusion mapping is a solved table. R3-03's NPC tells will likely collapse the hiding meta. R3-04 is a novelty coordination game with linear, memorisable content: the Squad Busters / Boat Together failure pattern. For a 2-5 person team, procedural or modular content (R3-05) scales best; hand-authored houses or museums (R3-01, R3-03) and rivers (R3-04) are the content treadmill risk.
